History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
50-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents with a 5–6-day history of persistent dry cough, runny nose, chills, myalgias, and fatigue—consistent with an uncomplicated viral upper respiratory tract infection.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Continuous dry cough (day & night) for ~5–6 days; accompanied by rhinorrhea.  
• Course: Began suddenly; cough remains bothersome, causing nocturnal awakening. Runny nose persists.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Throat irritation secondary to coughing; no painful swallowing.  
  – Chills/shivers in bed; subjective fever (temperature not taken).  
  – Early transient diarrhea at symptom onset (resolved).  
  – Generalized myalgias (arms, legs) and marked fatigue/lethargy.  
• Denied symptoms: Productive sputum, ear pain/discharge, chest pain, baseline dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, urinary symptoms, skin rash.  
• Review of systems: As above; no additional positives reported.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – on Metformin; routine outpatient follow-up.  
• Hypertension – on Lisinopril; reported well controlled.  
• No other chronic illnesses disclosed.

Medications (home):  
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with partner; partner currently well.  
• Employment: IT developer; sedentary job. Missed 1 work-day due to illness, returned despite symptoms.  
• Tobacco: Former smoker, quit 6 months ago.  
• Alcohol: Wine on ~3 evenings/week, 2–3 glasses each occasion. Advised to reduce.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
• Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.  
• No other familial conditions reported.

Physical Examination:
(No in-person examination performed; teleconsult)  
• Vitals: Not obtained.  
• General appearance: Described fatigue and weakness (patient report).  
• No other examination findings documented.

Investigations:
• None ordered or reviewed during this consultation.

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1: Suspected viral upper respiratory tract infection
  • Assessment: 5–6 day history of dry cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias, chills; no red-flag features; chest clear by history; likely self-limiting viral illness.
  • Plan:
    – Conservative management: rest, adequate hydration, regular paracetamol as needed.  
    – Off-work advice: take additional 1–2 days off to recover; reassess ability to return next week.  
    – Safety-netting: If no improvement within 2–3 days, persistent fever, worsening cough, or new/worsening breathlessness, return for face-to-face review; possible need for chest exam and antibiotics.  
    – Seek urgent care if dyspnea or chest pain develops.

Issue 2: Chronic conditions (Type 2 DM & Hypertension)
  • Assessment: Controlled on Metformin and Lisinopril per patient; no acute concerns today.
  • Plan:
    – Continue current medications.  
    – Lifestyle counseling: reduce alcohol intake (target ≤2 glasses/week, then further reduction) to assist BP and glycemic control.  
    – Routine follow-up with primary care/diabetes team as scheduled.

Issue 3: Smoking cessation maintenance
  • Assessment: Quit 6 months ago; beneficial for overall health.
  • Plan:
    – Positive reinforcement and encouragement to remain abstinent.

General plan items:
• Provide information leaflet on viral URTI self-care and red-flag symptoms.  
• Arrange follow-up appointment if symptoms persist or worsen.
